      text: |

# A plain and a principal mark of one key on one page

This is the shape the milestone died on, and it is here forever (IP2). Before
the typeset-time channel, the plain mark emitted a bare `\index` command and
the principal one an encapsulated command, which makeindex refuses to reconcile
when the two share a page: it warns, and Quarto fails the render on that
warning. Now every locator of the key carries the same encapsulation, so there
is nothing left to conflict, and the two marks fold into one locator that the
registry then emphasizes.

A passing mention of [wyvern]{.index} and, in the same sentence and on the same
page, its principal discussion: [wyvern]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

A second passing mention of [wyvern]{.index}, a page later, which must stay
plain.

# A principal mark inside a footnote

A footnote's `\index` command is written by the same deferred-to-shipout
mechanism the registration uses, so the two name the same page even though the
mark is typeset in a different box from the one it was written in.[^naga]

[^naga]: The principal discussion of [naga]{.index mention="principal"} lives in
    this note.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A registered page folded inside a makeindex range

makeindex folds three or more consecutive pages under one encapsulation into a
range, and the registry looks a page up by the string the index prints, which a
range does not match. So this term's principal page prints unemphasized — the
one silent degradation this back-end has, documented in README and left to M21,
which is where page ranges are taken up.

The first mention: [oni]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The principal discussion, on the next page: [oni]{.index mention="principal"}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

The last mention, on the page after that: [oni]{.index}.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# The control this fixture must leave alone

A term with no role anywhere, marked twice: [pixie]{.index} here,

{{< pagebreak >}}

and [pixie]{.index} a page later. Neither locator may be marked, and the
document may carry no registration for it at all.
